field_deviations.name: printing-preference-on-name-hits
field_deviations.note: SAME CARD, DIFFERENT PRINTING — the prefer_score divergence the 2026-08-16 differential sweep recorded as N9, surfacing on a name-route hit. `fuzzy=sol rin` resolves Sol Ring on both sides; Scryfall answers msc/213 and the mirror answers msc/211. The paths here are PRINTING identity only, deliberately: name, oracle_id, type_line, oracle_text, cmc, colors, legalities and the rest are still byte-compared, so a wrong CARD fails this case. Scryfall's preference is not derivable from what is stored here — probed on six flavor names with several carriers, it picks the lowest collector number three times, the newest release once, and a promo digital printing over a paper non-promo one once (prm/80925 over iko/377) — so this stays a recorded divergence rather than a guess.

field_deviations.name: same-name-different-card-on-a-name-hit
field_deviations.note: TWO CARDS SHARE ONE NAME, and the lanes pick different ones. `fuzzy=countersp` answers `Counters` on both sides — fmsc/9 (oracle 48f0cd77) on Scryfall, ftla/6 (oracle 14994561) here — two distinct oracle cards printed under the same name on two front-card sets. The fuzzy rule both sides implement is that names, not cards, compete, so neither answer is ambiguous and neither is wrong; which one wins is the same printing-preference question the sweep recorded as N9, one level up. THE CORPUS GAP THIS ENTRY USED TO RECORD IS CLOSED: those printings are imported now and carry `is:extra`, so `/cards/named?fuzzy=counters` answers `Counters`, `fuzzy=lightning` answers `Lightning` (fjmp/21) and `fuzzy=welcome australia` answers `Welcome to Australia` (unk) — all three were 404s or wrong cards before.

field_deviations.name: rulings-same-date-order
field_deviations.note: PRE-EXISTING, LANGUAGE-INDEPENDENT and already in the README's deviations list. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-16 and it does NOT close: the candidate fix was to preserve the rulings bulk file's row order within a date, on the theory that the dump is exported in internal-id order. Tested against api.scryfall.com over 25 cards that have both several dates and a date carrying 4+ rulings, the file's order matched 0 of 25 — as did that order reversed, whole-file order, date-ascending-then-file, and the comment rule this port ships. The reason is direct: the six shared 'kicker' rulings come back in a DIFFERENT order on different cards (Strength of Night, Goblin Barrage and Spell Contortion each get their own permutation of the same six comments), so Scryfall orders by a per-(card, ruling) row id rather than a per-ruling one, and the dump — one line per pair, grouped by card — cannot reproduce that within a card. So date desc + comment stays, and determinism is load-bearing beyond tidiness: identical bucket bytes are what let the publisher skip rewrites against the 1,000-writes/day budget. Both sides return the SAME 26 rulings for mom/230 in a different order; the array LENGTH is still compared (an array-length diff is not covered by this path), so a missing or extra ruling still fails. Nothing to do with the foreign id — /cards/<the English id>/rulings differs identically. rulings-en-jotun-grunt passes because that card has no crowded date.

cases.name: search-order-edhrec-desc-unranked-first

volatile_order.note: The two sides do not hold the same NUMBERS for this column, so `data` is compared by rule and not by position — see checkVolatileOrder in scripts/live-parity.ts for the four rules and why each one survives the churn.

cases.note:
THE ANCHOR FOR THE NULL-RANK PLACEMENT, and the one page where it is visible. `order=edhrec` is the DEFAULT orderby, and a missing EDHREC rank used to sort as the LOWEST value here — first ascending, last descending — because `perm_primary_key` gave every column one absent side. api.scryfall.com does the opposite for a RANK: this page leads with 33 unranked printings and then runs downward, while ascending page 1 holds no null at all in its 175 rows. Descending is the direction that fits the evidence on ONE page, which is why the case is `dir=desc`: ascending puts the nulls at the far end of 425 rows, three pages away, where a page-1 comparison would pass against either rule. Generation 37 rebuilt the stored permutation; before it, this page opened with our highest real rank (29937 in this store) where Scryfall opens with 33 unranked rows, so the two disagreed on the first 33 ids.

WHY IT IS `volatile_order` AND NOT A POSITIONAL COMPARISON. `edhrec_rank` is not merely volatile in VALUE — the two sides are ranking against DIFFERENT DUMPS, and the disagreement reaches the ORDER. Measured 2026-08-17: `Infernal Pet` is 25740 on api.scryfall.com and 25733 here, while `Runeforge Champion` is 25731 there and 25740 here. Each side is correctly sorted by its own numbers and the two pages still put the pair in opposite orders. All ten positional differences on that page were exactly this — four adjacent blocks, every one a pair the two snapshots rank in opposite directions — and Scryfall refreshes daily, so a position-for-position comparison fails forever with nothing to fix.

WHAT IS STILL PINNED, and it is more than the case asserted before: the 33-row unranked block id for id (which no snapshot skew can move, since an unranked row has no number to drift); that both sides are monotone descending in their OWN ranks; that every pair the two snapshots agree about strictly is ordered the same way by both pages (9,995 pairs asserted, 16 exempt on 2026-08-17); and — because the two `data` arrays are aligned by id before the byte comparison — every field of all 175 card objects, exactly as before. What is NOT asserted is the relative order of rows the two snapshots cannot separate, which is the only thing the churn can move and the only thing this case never meant to pin.

known_deviation.reason:
NOT AN ORDERING DEFECT, AND NOT A PARAMETER SCRYFALL IMPLEMENTS. Four sweep findings traced here; this entry closes them so nobody reinvestigates it as a sort bug.

THE EVIDENCE, measured 2026-08-17 in six serial requests to api.scryfall.com over `e:khm unique=prints` (425 rows). `order=cubecobra` is BYTE-IDENTICAL to `order=name` in BOTH directions — raw bodies equal, same 425 ids in the same sequence, and `next_page` on the cubecobra response carries `order=name`, not `order=cubecobra`.

AND THE FALLBACK IS NOT SPECIFIC TO `cubecobra`, which is the measurement that settles what to do about it. `order=elo` — a value invented for this test that no one documents — comes back byte-identical to both of them, 425 rows, `next_page` order=name, no warning. Meanwhile `order=review`, which Scryfall DOES document, answers a genuinely different order (Battlefield Raptor, Codespell Cleric, Usher of the Fallen) and echoes `order=review`. So api.scryfall.com does not accept `cubecobra` and decline to implement it: it does not RECOGNISE it, and silently coerces every unrecognised order to `name`, exactly as it does a typo.

THE DECISION IS TO KEEP OUR IMPLEMENTATION, deliberately, and the byte-identity above is why rather than why not.
  1. Matching the fallback would not be matching a documented Scryfall behaviour. It would be matching Scryfall's UNKNOWN-PARAMETER COERCION, which the `elo` probe shows is all this is.
  2. This route already implements that coercion. `order=elo` here answers 200 sorted by name, same as Scryfall. `cubecobra` diverges only because this project RECOGNISES the word. To match, the vocabulary would have to be made smaller on purpose — to forget a word it knows — and no rule in this repo asks for that.
  3. Parity's purpose is that a client written against api.scryfall.com gets the same answer here. No such client sends `order=cubecobra`: Scryfall neither documents it nor treats it as anything but a typo, so there is no reason for one to exist. The only caller who sends it is written against THIS project, and that caller wants the ordering.
  4. The cost is not zero. `cubecobra_score` is a corpus-global PERCENT_RANK over the distinct card names of the whole corpus (engine/wasm-import/src/lib.rs), stored as a column and sorted on. Matching the fallback would strand that pipeline to win byte-parity on a query nobody makes.
  5. And the asymmetry runs one way. A caller who wanted name order can ask for `order=name` and get byte-identical answers from both sides; a caller who wanted cubecobra order has no other way to ask.

`next_page` ECHOING `cubecobra` IS PART OF THE SAME DECISION, not a second one: page 1 comes back in cubecobra order, so a `next_page` that said `order=name` would page 2 by name and split one result set across two orderings. scripts/parity-sweep.ts classifies this UNSUPPORTED for the same reason.

ONE ADJACENT DIVERGENCE, RECORDED HERE AND NOT CHASED: on an order it does not recognise this route emits a `warnings` array ("Unrecognized order 'elo'; sorted by name instead.") where api.scryfall.com emits none. That is about UNKNOWN orders, not about `cubecobra`, and it is not what these four findings were.

WHAT EACH SIDE IS HELD TO. Scryfall's recording is its name-order answer, which is fully determined and cannot drift; if it ever stops matching `order=name`, Scryfall has started implementing something. Ours records that data.0 is NOT the name-order row. A change to `Village Rites` there is DRIFT, not a failure, and means the nightly cubecobra table moved — re-measure and re-record.

cases.name: search-color-name-guild-azorius
cases.note: The guild/shard/wedge colour vocabulary. `c:azorius` was a 400 here until 2026-08-16 -- the parser knew only white/blue/black/red/green/colorless and bare letter strings -- while Scryfall answers the same 6 cards `c:wu` does. The 44 names and their letter spellings were measured pair by pair over the whole corpus (see COLOR_ALIAS_TO_CODES) because Kaldheim holds one card of three colours or more and would have agreed with almost any mapping.

cases.name: search-color-name-shard-bant
cases.note: `id:`/`identity:`/`ci:` take the same vocabulary `c:` does, measured separately rather than assumed: id:bant e:khm == id:gwu e:khm == 176.

cases.name: search-color-name-four-color-hyphenated
cases.note: The four-colour names are HYPHENATED, and `-` is not a word-continuation character, so the lexer sees WORD MINUS WORD and the parser has to glue them back. `yore` alone is REJECTED by Scryfall, so the un-hyphenated nickname is deliberately not in the table.

cases.name: search-typographic-quotes-fold
cases.note: U+201C/U+201D and U+2019 fold to ASCII quotes before lexing -- and the curly apostrophe INSIDE the double quotes folds too, which is the only reason this finds the card. The fold used to live on the compat surface alone, so /search and the web UI rejected the very quotes their own search box produces; it now lives in the parser (src/parser/tokenizer.ts).

cases.name: search-dangling-operator-is-a-bare-word
cases.note: A keyword with no value is not a term at all: `t:` is the bare word `t`, and a bare word is a name search. This port answered `t: e:khm` with all 323 of Kaldheim (an always-true leaf); Scryfall answers the 215 whose NAME contains a t, which is exactly `t e:khm` and `name:t e:khm`.

cases.name: search-dangling-operator-negated
cases.note: The negation composes because the rewrite produces an ordinary term: 323 - 215 = 108, and `-t e:khm` is 108 on Scryfall too.

cases.name: search-face-colours-mdfc-colorless
cases.note: A colour comparison runs over the FACES' masks, not the merged row's union. This is the whole set of MDFCs with a colourless face -- almost all of them land backs -- and the port answered 12 of the 61 before gen 29, because the union of a white front and a colourless back is white. Kept as a LIST rather than one card so a partial fix cannot pass it.

cases.name: search-face-colours-split-card-is-not-colourless
cases.note: THE REGRESSION GUARD, and the reason OracleFace.card_colors is an Option. A split face carries no `colors` key at all -- Fire // Ice's two halves have name, mana_cost and type_line and nothing more -- so a per-face read that treats an absent key as the mask 0 answers 1 here where Scryfall answers 404, and every split and flip card in the corpus becomes colourless. An absent key inherits the card's mask; a DECLARED `"colors": []` (an MDFC land back) really is colourless. Answers 404 on both sides, which is what the empty-list case above cannot check.

cases.name: search-face-colours-union-is-not-a-value
cases.note: The other direction, which the stat columns do not have: the merged colour value is a UNION, so it is a value no face holds, and matching against it OVER-matches. Extus's faces are {W,B} and {B,R}; only the union is {W,B,R}, so `c:brw` answered 1 here and 404 on Scryfall. `c=3` on the same card is the same fact through the colour count.

cases.name: search-face-colours-front-face-alone
cases.note: The under-matching direction, on an exact comparison: Valki is mono-black and Tibalt is {B,R}, so `c=b` is satisfied by the front face alone and by no union. Pinned beside the over-matching case above because a fix for either one on its own is wrong.

cases.name: search-date-bare-year-is-the-year
cases.note: A PARTIAL DATE IS A RANGE. `date:2021` means "released in 2021", and this port answered 0 -- the engine zero-padded the value to 20210000 and compared that one point, so nothing was ever equal to it. The padded reading is the START of the window, which is the right bound for `<` and `>=` and wrong for the other four operators; each now reads the end it needs. `date:<year>` and `year:<year>` agree on all seven spellings, exactly, which is the check that matters -- `year:` was correct all along.

cases.name: search-date-bare-year-negated
cases.note: The residual the negated-comparison work left behind: `-date:2021` is 141 on Scryfall because `date` DISCARDS the minus and applies the term positively, and it was 0 here only because our own positive form was broken. Both halves now agree, so this pins the two rules together -- the minus rule and the range rule -- rather than either alone.

cases.name: search-unknown-keyword-under-a-comparison-is-not-ignored
cases.note: `nonsense:1` is ignored-and-warned; `nonsense>=1` is a 404 with NO warnings key. Scryfall's value validators and its unknown-keyword table are not reached by `>` `>=` `<` `<=` `!=` at all -- the term is honored and matches nothing. This port ignored-and-warned both, answering 151 with a warning Scryfall does not emit.

cases.name: search-comparison-on-a-text-column-matches-nothing
cases.note: The same rule from the other side, which is why it is one rule and not two: a comparison operator on a TEXT column is honored and matches nothing, exactly as it is on a keyword nobody knows. The boundary was enumerated -- every DB_COLUMNS alias and every directive name probed as `<alias>>=0 e:khm t:creature` -- and only the numeric columns, the colour family, mana, produces, rarity, date and devotion compare at all. This port did a real lexicographic comparison and answered 54.

cases.name: search-rarity-checks-its-value-under-a-comparison
cases.note: Rarity is an ordered enum, so `r>rare` is a comparison Scryfall really performs -- and it therefore checks the value under a comparison exactly as it does under `:`. All seven of `r:notarare` through `r!=notarare` answer 151 with the same sentence (whose full stop sits INSIDE the closing quote, which is Scryfall's). With an equality-only guard this port answered `400 Failed to parse query`.

cases.name: search-devotion-checks-its-value
cases.note: Devotion takes one colour repeated or one hybrid PAIR repeated; anything else is ignored-and-warned, in both polarities and under every operator. There was no devotion validator here at all, so `devotion>2` reached the engine and answered 149. `{p}` and `{}` earn a different sentence -- `Unknown mana symbols` -- because those are not symbols Scryfall recognises, where `{c}`, `{s}`, `{x}`, `{1}`, `{2/r}` and `{r/p}` are symbols that simply are not devotion.

cases.name: search-devotion-hybrid-sums-its-two-colours
cases.note: A hybrid devotion value asks about BOTH its colours as one quantity: the measure is the sum of the queried lanes. This expanded {R/G} to lanes r=1,g=1 and compared per lane, which means "a red pip AND a green pip" -- 1 card, against Scryfall's 62 (= 27 + 36 - the one KHM creature carrying both).

cases.name: search-devotion-hybrid-is-a-sum-not-a-per-lane-or
cases.note: The row that tells a SUM from a per-lane OR, and the reason the headline count above is not enough evidence on its own. `devotion:{r}{r}` is 7 and `devotion:{g}{g}` is 8, so an OR over the lanes cannot exceed 15 -- this is 16. The sixteenth card has one red pip and one green pip, so neither lane reaches 2 while the sum does.

cases.name: search-devotion-equality-reads-only-the-queried-colours
cases.note: `devotion={r}` is d[r] == 1 with the other colours FREE: 20, which is `devotion:{r}`'s 27 less `devotion:{r}{r}`'s 7. This compared the whole six-lane vector for equality, pinning every unqueried colour to zero, and so answered 15 -- it excluded every red card that is also green.

cases.name: search-mana-generic-is-a-counted-pip
cases.note: `{2}` in a mana value is two GENERIC pips, not cmc 2. Numeric symbols carry no lane, so a cost's generic survived only inside cmc and every coloured pip paid for it; this answered 142 (cards with cmc >= 2) against Scryfall's 102.

cases.name: search-mana-generic-is-not-cmc
cases.note: The decisive case, and it is not in KHM -- no KHM creature costs exactly {R}{R}. A {R}{R} cost has cmc 2 and generic 0, so Scryfall answers 0 here while `m={r}{r} t:creature` alone answers 24. Comparing cmc matched all 24.

cases.name: search-mana-bare-generic-is-not-an-empty-cost
cases.note: The unbraced shorthand: `m:2` is `m:{2}`, both 102. The value reaches the engine as the string "2", and the cmc parser reads braces and bare letters but not loose digits -- so this arrived as the EMPTY cost, which is a tautology, and answered all 151.

cases.name: search-equals-on-a-text-column-is-a-substring
cases.note: `=` on a text column is `:`, not an equality -- 32 either way. This compared the whole oracle text for equality and answered 0. Distinct from the ordered comparisons (`o>flying` and friends), which really do match nothing, and from `!=`, which is the empty set.

cases.name: search-equals-on-a-collection-column-is-membership
cases.note: Same rule on a collection column: `kw=flying` is `kw:flying`, 28. Set EQUALITY is not a meaning Scryfall gives `=` here -- this answered 9, the cards whose ONLY keyword is Flying. The colour columns are the boundary and keep a real equality: `c=rg` is 1 against `c:rg`'s 2.

cases.name: search-date-year-month-is-that-month
cases.note: A partial date names a WINDOW one precision below the bare year: `date:2021-02` is February 2021, and equals `date>=2021-02 date<2021-03`. The parser consumed the month looking for a day and, finding none, returned the bare year -- silently dropping tokens it had already eaten -- so this answered the whole of 2021.

cases.name: search-unique-cards-khm-gods
cases.note: `e:khm t:god` asked under all three uniques on 2026-08-17, and the PAIRING is the point rather than any one count: without it a future reader cannot tell which mechanism moved a changed `unique=art` number. `unique=cards` is 13 -- the twelve paper gods plus `khm/A-40` A-Alrund, which is a different CARD and so a row of its own -- and it byte-compares clean, A-* row included.

cases.name: search-unique-prints-khm-gods
cases.note: The second half of that pairing: `unique=prints` is 26, those 13 cards' printings, byte-clean in the same order. So the corpus, the collector-number sort key and the Alchemy A-* rows all agree with api.scryfall.com under both uniques, and the ONLY thing that can move `unique=art` off 26 is the artwork dedupe itself -- which is what makes search-unique-art-khm-gods a statement about SCOPE and not about the store. Both counts are unmoved by 5d86e76's key change (`unique=printing` and `unique=card` do not move in either space).

known_deviation.reason:
The one unique of the three that moves, and it moves by exactly one row: `khm/A-40`. Scryfall dedupes an artwork ACROSS cards, and A-Alrund carries Alrund's front and back illustrations unchanged, so its 26 printings collapse to 25 with the A-* row as the one that goes. This port's scope is PER-CARD — 5d86e76 made the key the whole face tuple, c7d8cf3 measured that dropping oracle_id from the scope reproduces both of Scryfall's numbers exactly (26 -> 25 here, 187 -> 174 on znr), and 5440875 deferred the change on purpose — so A-Alrund keeps an artwork of its own and this answers 26.
WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED: closing the scope needs a corpus-wide dense artwork id in place of `artwork_base[card] + gid`, a cross-partition dedupe in the gather (cross-card groups must be co-located in one partition to keep `unique=art` a per-partition row predicate, and today's partitioning is `fnv1a64/oracle_id/v1`), a deterministic tie-break on row identity that the per-card scope provably never needed, and a representative rule that search-unique-art-znr-creatures proves is not derivable at all. Sized on the served store it buys 102 cross-oracle groups over 417 rows.
WHAT EACH SIDE STILL PROVES: both sides lead with khm/15 in the same order and differ only from data.3 on, where Scryfall has already dropped A-40 and moved khm/50 up. The sibling cases pin `unique=cards` 13 and `unique=prints` 26 byte-clean, so a change in the 25 or the 26 here is the artwork rule and nothing else.
NOTE FOR A RUN AGAINST PRODUCTION: the deployed store has the Alchemy A-* rows missing from its search space entirely, and therefore answers 25 for a reason that has nothing to do with artwork. This case is written against the LOCAL corpus, the one the rest of this file already assumes (see search-include-multilingual-khm-page-1's 4035).

known_deviation.reason:
TWO mechanisms in one total, and only one of them is closable. 187 here against 174 on api.scryfall.com, a difference of exactly the 13 Alchemy rows znr/A-68, A-105, A-126, A-141, A-145, A-154, A-185, A-187, A-198, A-224, A-228, A-234 and A-238, which Scryfall folds into their paper originals by the same CROSS-CARD dedupe as search-unique-art-khm-gods.
THE OTHER FIVE ROWS ARE A PER-CARD REPRESENTATIVE CHOICE, AND IT IS NOT DERIVABLE — this is the half no scope change can reach. On five artworks the two sides keep different survivors: this engine answers znr/4, znr/23, znr/198, znr/220 and znr/225 where Scryfall answers znr/315, znr/318, znr/361, znr/365 and znr/367. Measured on 2026-08-17 by asking `e:znr t:creature` twice — `unique=prints` 230 rows against `unique=art` 174 — and labelling every merge. 39 of them are ONE shape: a base printing against its extended-art twin, agreeing on oracle_id, illustration_id, set, `released_at`, artist, rarity and frame effects, differing only in `extendedart`/`boosterfun` and the collector number. 35 resolve to the base printing and 4 to the extended-art one. znr/198 loses to znr/361 as well, in a three-row group that is not one of the 39, which is why the result differs on 5 rows and not 4. znr/5 against znr/316 is byte-for-byte the same comparison as znr/4 against znr/315 and goes the OTHER way.
An exhaustive sweep over every key api.scryfall.com puts on the card object finds no field whose ordering picks the winner and — the stronger statement — no field whose base-vs-extended delta even SEPARATES the 4 from the 35. Narrowed to a single pair the answer does not move: `e:znr (cn:4 or cn:315) unique=art` is still znr/315, `(cn:2 or cn:314)` is znr/2, `(cn:198 or cn:361)` is znr/361. So it is a fixed internal ordinal on Scryfall's side — `DISTINCT ON` over the filtered set against row identity in their own table — and not query noise, and nothing they publish exposes it. `prefer_score` DESC, what `group_representative` already uses, agrees with 58 of the 65 live-labelled decisions and no available alternative does better, so it stays. DO NOT re-derive this: the dead end has been walked to its end twice (c7d8cf3 over the bulk, 5440875 over the API), and it is here so nobody walks it a third time.
The recorded rows are the FIRST divergence on each side (data.2, the znr/4-against-znr/315 merge) plus the block Scryfall's five winners occupy, so a change in either the scope or the representative rule reports as drift.

cases.name: search-unique-art-null-back-keeps-both-itlimoc
cases.note: The positive half of the face-tuple artwork key (5d86e76): an artwork is the ordered tuple of EVERY face's illustration id, not the front alone. Seven printings collapse to five on both sides, and the row that proves the key is `alci/26` against `lci/188` -- one front (`d097bf4c`) with two different backs (`92726e09` against `a4cc664f`) -- which a front-only key merges into a single artwork. The controls sit in the same answer: `lci/380` carries lci/188's tuple exactly and does merge, and `xln/191` + `pxln/191s` share (807e1577, fe41f4ca) and merge, while `pxtc/191` keeps that same front against back `7cec268a` and survives. Both sides agree on all five representatives, so this byte-compares rather than deviating -- and it is the reason `unique=art`'s scope question (search-unique-art-khm-gods) is about SCOPE and not about the key.

cases.name: search-unique-art-prismatic-ending
cases.note: The guard half of the same key, and what keeps the tuple from being a 161-row regression: an ABSENT illustration id is UNKNOWN, not a value. Eleven printings collapse to seven on both sides. `amh2/5` and `amh2/5s` are art-series rows carrying no illustration id at all, and an all-absent tuple matches only its own kind at the same arity -- so the two become ONE artwork. A literal tuple that read NULL as a value would answer 8; an all-absent row treated as a wildcard that folds into whichever artwork its card listed first would answer 6. The rest is ordinary front sharing and is here to keep the count honest: mb2/16 + mh2/25 + mh2/384 on `78feeb10`, soa/72 + soa/137 on `7d772ba3`, and pf26/3, sld/1868, soa/7 and spg/40 alone. (The third leg, a PARTIAL wildcard -- astx/66s's `(b7de5431, NULL)` against astx/66's `(b7de5431, c9d340c9)`, the 161 art-series signature variants -- is not pinned here: `!"Memory Lapse" include:extras unique=art` is 9 on both sides and drops astx/66s on both, but seven of its nine representatives are the per-card choice search-unique-art-znr-creatures records as underivable, so a case on it would be a large deviation and not a guard.)
